text:
Zach Hyman picked up his 500th career point on Nov. 15 in Philadelphia, a go-ahead goal, which is a nice number for a fifth-round pick who made his name doing the hard work in front of the net for Toronto and then Edmonton. He's played 13 games, with a stretch out between late October and early November, and has 4 goals and 6 points.

The finishing is fine; his shooting is right where we'd expect. What's down is the volume of chances. His own chance quality is 1.26 expected goals per 60 minutes, well off the 1.82 that drove his 31 goals in 58 games last season, and at five on five the Oilers are taking only 47% of the expected goals with him on the ice. His minutes have also dipped by almost three a night over his last ten games.

Evolving-Hockey had him at the 98th percentile among forwards for driving play last season, with a caution that strong linemates flatter his raw numbers. At 34, the question for the rest of the season is simple: does he get back to the crease often enough to score like Hyman? That's what we'd watch.
headline: Zach Hyman reaches 500 and keeps grinding
